sentences.text: The leader of the Jewish Greens, Vivien Lichtenstein, said on Friday he should resign, adding it was a "big mistake" for him to have dodged a debate about a party conference motion that declared Zionism a form of racism.
sentences.article_title: Polanski vows to stay on as Green leader as he faces criticism after by-election defeat

sentences.text: Lichtenstein's comments come after two former Green leaders accused Polanski of failing to show leadership over the Zionism row.
sentences.article_title: Polanski vows to stay on as Green leader as he faces criticism after by-election defeat

sentences.text: Polanski, who came second to Labour overnight in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election, told BBC Breakfast he would "absolutely" stay on as leader and "of course" had not questioned that.
sentences.article_title: Polanski vows to stay on as Green leader as he faces criticism after by-election defeat

sentences.text: The Greens had hoped to take the seat, previously held by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer, after a by-election success earlier this year .
sentences.article_title: Polanski vows to stay on as Green leader as he faces criticism after by-election defeat

sentences.text: Polanski lost out in Thursday's contest in London to Labour candidate Sagal Abdi-Wali, who secured 45% of the vote to his 33% - but the Green vote share was up by 22 percentage points on the 2024 general election.
sentences.article_title: Polanski vows to stay on as Green leader as he faces criticism after by-election defeat

sentences.text: The motion, which was passed by rank-and-file members to become official party policy, defined Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state" and backed a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine", which includes modern-day Israel.
sentences.article_title: Polanski vows to stay on as Green leader as he faces criticism after by-election defeat

sentences.text: Adrian Ramsay, a Green MP and former co-leader, declined to back Polanski when asked on the BBC's Politics East on Friday.

sentences.text: "A lot depends on what happens in the days and weeks to come," he replied when asked if Polanski should still lead the party.
sentences.article_title: Polanski vows to stay on as Green leader as he faces criticism after by-election defeat

sentences.text: "[He] did not show leadership I would have been looking for," said Ramsay, who said he was now working to reverse the motion.

sentences.text: Polanski defended his absence from the controversial motion vote in Brighton, saying he was busy campaigning in the North London constituency.

sentences.text: Kelly Kershaw stole from vulnerable customers to fund several expensive holidays A building society cashier who stole thousands of pounds from customers to pay for "lavish" holidays has been ordered to repay more than £12,000.
sentences.article_title: Bank cashier outed by holiday photos after stealing £13k is ordered to pay back money

sentences.text: Kelly Kershaw, 54, stole £13,333 including from vulnerable and elderly customers at Nationwide in Caernarfon, Gwynedd, even forging the signature of a man with learning disabilities.
sentences.article_title: Bank cashier outed by holiday photos after stealing £13k is ordered to pay back money

sentences.text: Kershaw admitted five counts of fraud after colleagues spotted Facebook posts of her on safari in Africa, and on trips to Paris, Tuscany and Dubai.
sentences.article_title: Bank cashier outed by holiday photos after stealing £13k is ordered to pay back money

sentences.text: She was jailed for 16 months in May but returned to Caernarfon Crown Court for a Proceeds of Crime Act , external hearing, and told to pay back £12,630 - the amount of money she had in assets.
sentences.article_title: Bank cashier outed by holiday photos after stealing £13k is ordered to pay back money

sentences.text: Judge Jones ordered Kershaw to repay the sum within three months or face a further five months in prison.
sentences.article_title: Bank cashier outed by holiday photos after stealing £13k is ordered to pay back money

sentences.text: The mother-of-two posted pictures of skiing trips, safaris and romantic European getaways on her Facebook page and boasted she was "living and loving life one adventure at a time".
sentences.article_title: Bank cashier outed by holiday photos after stealing £13k is ordered to pay back money

sentences.text: Kershaw's victims included an 85-year-old man who had lost some "cognitive abilities" after suffering a stroke - and she stole £6,300 from him.

sentences.text: The review looks at NHS waiting times and whether young people are being over-diagnosed.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: It has been called a "generational opportunity" to rethink support for both mental health conditions and ADHD and autism.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The review, commissioned by then-health secretary Wes Streeting 10 months ago after saying young people were being "over-diagnosed" and "written off", could have major implications for NHS services, the benefits system, schools and employment support.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Its 600-plus pages , external contain a host of conclusions and recommendations.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Here are the key takeaways.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The report is clear that there is an increasing risk of over-diagnosis, but only when it comes to ADHD and autism.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Experts said a rise in diagnoses over the past 25 years meant cases now appear to be outstripping the expected number in the population for some younger age groups.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: They gave the example of children aged six to 17 – more than 4% have been diagnosed with autism.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: That's well above the 1-2% that studies suggest is the true level.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: But this comes with a big caveat.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: There are weaknesses in the data.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Evidence about the true level of autism relies on surveys that have not been done for nine years, so the review team have had to estimate what has happened since.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: And there are some age groups where these conditions are still being under-diagnosed, and that should not be overlooked.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: It is why the review team said it could not yet conclude over-diagnosis was happening "at scale".
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: But there is certainly evidence to suggest we are moving from an era of under-diagnosis to one of over-diagnosis, the experts said.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: They warn not every difficulty requires a medical response and there is a risk of blurring the lines between diagnosable ADHD and autism and what should be considered the "normal human variation in brain function, cognition and behaviour".
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Where the review team very clearly rejects the idea of over-diagnosis is with mental health.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: In fact, the chair, Prof Peter Fonagy, has said Streeting was "completely wrong" on that.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: He said the increase in mental distress is real – one in four 16 to 24-year-olds are now thought to experience it, up from one in six 30 years ago.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: He links this to a variety of factors including economic uncertainty, the impact of social media and loss of youth services.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: This contrasts with autism and ADHD.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: While diagnoses have increased, the true level in the whole population (regardless of whether they have come forward or not) has remained broadly stable, according to best estimates.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: What is not happening with mental health, though, is an increase in severe mental illness.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Population rates of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, for example, have remained stable.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Instead, what is driving the rise is conditions such as anxiety, depression, self-harm and eating disorders.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Where the review experts share, to some extent, Streeting's concerns is on the impact of diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: They said there was a risk it ends up closing doors to opportunities.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: It can, they said, act as a label that defines them by their "difficulties" rather than "strengths and potential".
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: This then hampers them in education, work and relationships.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Around a third of 16 to 24-year-olds not in education, employment or training (NEET) report their mental health or autism as a factor.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Those diagnosed with ADHD before the age of 17 are four times more likely to be a NEET than those without.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Addressing this, they said, would require better support post-diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Some of that is down to the NHS, but as important is the approach of schools, workplaces and wider society.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Another area where the review team is united in its view is that the support system is "falling short" of what people need for both mental health and neurological conditions such as ADHD and autism.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Waiting times for assessment are too long.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: A third of young people referred to mental health services wait more than a year, while of the 900,000 people waiting for ADHD or autism checks, 90% have waited more than three months.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: In the lead up to publication of the report, NHS Alliance, which represents health bosses, said the system was in chaos.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: But this goes further than the NHS.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The report said support across care, education, employment and welfare remains fragmented, with people having to "jump through hoops" and face repeated assessment and conflicting requirements to get support.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: No time should be wasted in tackling these challenges, the review says.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: On long waits, it says everyone on a waiting list should be reassessed so that those most in need are prioritised for help.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: There should no longer be a first-come, first-served approach.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Some of those waiting may benefit from non-medical support, advice about sleeping better or getting more physical exercise, for example.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: That may even lead to some being removed from the waiting list.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: There should also be better assessments before people are placed on waiting lists too.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Not every problem needs a medical solution, the experts make clear.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Quality and consistency of autism and ADHD assessments must be improved, with the review highlighting concerns about those done by the private sector on behalf of the NHS.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Half of ADHD and a third of autism assessments are done by non-NHS providers, such as charities and private firms.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: But they are not subject to the same regulation as NHS providers – and this must change.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The experts also said it wanted to see a ban on direct-to-public advertising of assessments.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The review has said it wants to see action over the next 12 to 24 months.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The government has promised to act – and is expected to set out more details in its forthcoming mental health strategy which is expected by the end of the year.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: But now she says she simply lets it out: "If someone catcalls me in the street, I rage.

sentences.text: I don't care." From the workplace to popular culture, experts say women like Galea, 34, are increasingly expressing their anger more openly than before.

sentences.text: Elon Musk (right) has accused the Ambanis of blocking Starlink's entry into India Elon Musk has questioned whether billionaire Mukesh Ambani is the "real boss of India" as his satellite internet company Starlink struggles to secure final approval to launch in the country.

sentences.text: A second head teachers' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections in England, saying it is "increasingly concerned about the welfare and morale" of its members.

sentences.text: Andy Burnham has promised to curb companies' ability to restrict what their workers can do after leaving their job.
sentences.article_title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts

sentences.text: In a speech, the prime minister said the use of non-compete clauses in employment contracts had "gone too far" and was holding innovative UK companies back.
sentences.article_title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts

sentences.text: He added the clauses had forced workers to go without pay after leaving a role, as well as making it harder for growing firms to hire new staff.
sentences.article_title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts

sentences.text: Ahead of the Budget later this month, he also said there was "more to do" on tax to encourage promising firms to stay in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts

sentences.text: Sir Keir Starmer's government had been exploring possible restrictions on non-compete clauses since late last year, including a total ban, banning them above a certain salary threshold, or limiting how long they can last.
sentences.article_title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts

sentences.text: Although commonly associated with the financial services and technology sectors, research cited by the government has estimated around 5 million jobs in Britain are covered by the clauses, typically lasting around six months.
sentences.article_title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts

sentences.text: Speaking at a business summit in Manchester, Burnham confirmed his government would press ahead with new legislation to ensure the clauses can "no longer be a barrier" to hiring new staff.
sentences.article_title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts

sentences.text: Burnham did not specify the scope of the restrictions he is planning, but suggested they would apply to the "everyday economy" as well as helping "promising start-ups and scaling firms".
sentences.article_title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts

sentences.text: It is understood that the government is planning to unveil details of the proposed restrictions, which were first reported by Politico , external and The Financial Times , external , alongside the Budget on 28 October.
sentences.article_title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts

sentences.text: Responding to the prime minister's comments, the Recruitment and Employment Confederation warned against "sweeping" changes to non-compete rules, adding they played a "vital role" in protecting commercially sensitive information and client relationships.
sentences.article_title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts

sentences.text: The previous Conservative government had ruled out a total ban , external on non-compete clauses, after hearing from employers that it could reduce investor confidence in the UK or prompt companies to tighten how they share information internally.
sentences.article_title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts

sentences.text: The prime minister sought to frame the announcement on non-compete clauses as part of a wider government pitch to boost innovative sectors of the economy.
sentences.article_title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts

sentences.text: He told the summit that although the UK was home to outstanding research and start-ups, too many companies had gone abroad in search of investment.
sentences.article_title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts

sentences.text: He also signalled that the government would "say more" at the Budget about plans to use public investment as a way to encourage private funding in the economy.
sentences.article_title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts

sentences.text: He added that he wanted all UK regions to have a dedicated fund to do this, modelled on the Good Growth Fund launched in Greater Manchester last year, during his tenure as mayor of the city-region.
sentences.article_title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts

sentences.text: He also hinted that the government was looking at the tax system to ensure the UK can retain high-growth companies.
sentences.article_title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts

sentences.text: He said: "One of our biggest challenges is breaking through our own ceiling.

sentences.text: Tobias White-Sansom died in a Spanish hospital in July 2022 Four years after watching his brother die in his arms, Maximilian White believes new evidence could help him get answers.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: Tobias White-Sansom, a father-of-two from Nottingham, died in a Spanish hospital in July 2022, five days after a night out in Magaluf, and his family believes the way security and police officers handled him that night led to his death.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: A blood spatter report and a court order received by the family this month have reignited their hopes that criminal proceedings could commence in the Spanish courts.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: White told the BBC: "I won't stop until we get justice for Toby." The 46-year-old medical cannabis entrepreneur said he found it difficult to talk about the way he lost his younger sibling, who was on a family holiday at the time.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: White-Sansom was pinned down at a nightclub following a row over him removing his T-shirt because he was too hot, his family said.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: They told the BBC the Spanish Civil Guard - the Guardia Civil - was called and he was handcuffed, Tasered and injected with tranquilisers before going into cardiac arrest.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: Tobias White-Sansom's brother said they were both born and raised in Nottingham The family believe the blood spatter evidence - which forms part of an ongoing investigation that will see a court judge decide whether a criminal case is warranted - could suggest external force was used.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: The report, which analysed White-Sansom's T-shirt, trainers and a sock, said several individual bloodstains were identified, which are compatible both with spatter stains caused through the application of an external force and with drip stains, produced by gravity.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: An ambulance report, seen by the BBC, states White-Sansom had taken drugs and was agitated.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: He was administered a number of medications including fentanyl, the report added.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: The Guardia Civil has not provided any further detail on the death.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: At the time it issued a statement, saying: "Upon the arrival of the Guardia Civil police, this man was violent and police reduced him to be assisted by medical services.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "He was taken to the hospital for treatment.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: There, once while he was being assisted, he was arrested for a crime of injury." White-Sansom was put in an induced coma Days later, White and the rest of the family were forced to make an agonising decision.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "The only thing keeping him alive was the life support machine," he recalled.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "And we discussed between our family members and we decided it was inhumane and we should let Toby die naturally.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "So then, my decision was to turn the machine off myself, and then my brother died in my arms.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "The doctors said he would slip away within five to six minutes, and Toby being the strong-willed person that he was, it took 11 minutes." White (left) says his brother should be here, caring for his family In the four years since, White said he had been trying to reach a resolution.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "The whole brutality of the situation caused my brother to pass," he said.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "Someone needs to be accountable.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: And also, for his children to know that he was a good person, not a drunk tourist in Magaluf." White said on the night in question, his teenage son wanted to go out but he did not want him to go by himself, so White-Sansom accompanied him along with his girlfriend.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "What never sat well with me was that my brother was not with a group of lads on a stag do," he said.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "It just didn't make sense.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: That's why I went so heavy in return, because I knew that's not how my brother lived and what he was about." A vigil in White-Sansom's memory gathered crowds in Nottingham city centre back in 2022 White spoke to the BBC days after receiving the evidence and a court order.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "The process is extremely gruesome because even when you're getting good news, it's bittersweet - my brother is still not here," he said.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "It's just the truth - fighting an uphill battle just to get the truth.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: At this point, it's a sweet picture but also bitter because Toby is not around." An inquest into White-Sansom's death was also opened in the UK in 2022, and paused while investigations in Spain continued.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: White believes the new evidence could significantly impact the process but if that fails, he says he will take the matter to the UK.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "The truth is out there, the evidence is there, we just need help putting it in front of the right people to get this justice for Toby that's needed," he said.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "When you lose a sibling, it's like losing your complete history of who you were and what you stood for," White says The family's lawyer in Spain told the BBC he had never seen a case like this before.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "I've never seen a case... with a whole package of circumstances and such a delay," said Jaime Campaner.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "I've never seen it and I hope I never see it again." He said he had been filing motion after motion to speed up the process, and said the Spanish Civil Guard - the Guardia Civil - was to blame for the delay.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: The Guardia Civil told the BBC the case was before the court and it had no further comment to make.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "The Spanish investigation has been very slow," Campaner added.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "And this is not common in a city like Palma, where investigations don't take so long." He said the investigating judge in Spain would now consider the new evidence, and decide whether to proceed as a criminal case or shelve it.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "We believe this could be key evidence.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: We are not aware of the conclusions yet but it might end in results [for] this case," he said.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: They are yet to be given a date for a court hearing but Campaner estimates the investigating stage would conclude by the end of the year, with a prospective court case starting next year.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "We all want to get this case closed and see some justice," said White.
sentences.article_title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain

sentences.text: "We're hoping that at some point in this chapter, we can close the door on this - and we can close the door on this pain." sentences.text: Drought was declared due to low water levels in reservoirs and rivers Drought has been declared across Yorkshire following months of unusually dry weather.
sentences.article_title: Drought declared in Yorkshire after dry weather

sentences.text: The Environment Agency (EA) said low water levels in reservoirs and rivers had triggered the move despite recent rainfall across parts of the region.
sentences.article_title: Drought declared in Yorkshire after dry weather

sentences.text: Yorkshire officially entered drought status on Friday after a lack of spring and summer rainfall, having previously been classified as in a period of prolonged dry weather.
sentences.article_title: Drought declared in Yorkshire after dry weather

sentences.text: Yorkshire Water said it was not planning to introduce water restrictions for customers at this stage despite the drought declaration.
sentences.article_title: Drought declared in Yorkshire after dry weather

sentences.text: Andy Shaw, head of water production, treatment and energy at Yorkshire Water, said the EA's decision reflected dry conditions across the region but "does not mean water restrictions are currently needed".
sentences.article_title: Drought declared in Yorkshire after dry weather

sentences.text: EA manager Vicki Townend said Yorkshire had seen its fifth driest period on record between April and September.
sentences.article_title: Drought declared in Yorkshire after dry weather

sentences.text: Townend said: "The ongoing lack of rainfall means the flow in rivers and groundwater levels in certain parts of our area are very low and have now reached our trigger for declaring a drought.
sentences.article_title: Drought declared in Yorkshire after dry weather

sentences.text: "As we see more impacts from climate change, heavier rainfall and drier summers will become more frequent.
sentences.article_title: Drought declared in Yorkshire after dry weather

sentences.text: "Long-term resilience against our changing climate is a priority for this government." Following the hottest and one of the driest summers on record, rainfall continued to be below average through September.

sentences.text: Thames Valley Police has accepted warrants it used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes at the time of his arrest in February were unlawful, the High Court has been told.

sentences.text: Following Thursday's hearing, items seized in the raid continue to be held by the police, with a further hearing to take place in 2027 to decide whether the material can be used as evidence.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the criminal investigation into Mountbatten-Windsor is ongoing.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: The former prince, who denies any wrongdoing, was arrested by police on 19 February on suspicion of misconduct in public office, after which he launched a legal challenge over the legality of the search warrants.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: The force said it accepted that the "initial court's decision to issue warrants under the specific piece of legislation used was incorrect" before they searched the properties.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: On Thursday at the High Court, judge Mr Justice Hilliard said Mountbatten-Windsor and the police had agreed that the search warrants had been unlawful.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: However, he added: "The fact that the search warrants were quashed does not bring the investigation to an end or mean that the whole of the investigation is unlawful." Mountbatten-Windsor opposes the police's bid to retain the evidence, the judge said, and another hearing is expected in 2027.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: Mountbatten-Windsor remains under police investigation despite a ruling that the way search warrants were issued was unlawful His lawyers have used a judicial review to challenge the actions of the force's chief constable and the Central Criminal Court in the build-up to his arrest.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: His arrest arose after the US Department of Justice published documents which raised suspicions he had forwarded confidential information to the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein when Mountbatten-Windsor was a UK trade envoy in 2010.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: He has consistently denied any wrongdoing in relation to Epstein.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: The court heard on Thursday that Thames Valley Police seized documents and electronic devices when they raided Mountbatten-Windsor's homes earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: Thames Valley Police's position was that they had applied for search warrants under section eight and nine of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 at a hearing at the Central Criminal Court the day before the search.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: That court determined that only section eight search warrants were needed and they were granted on that basis - but subsequently, a legal challenge has established that the court should have issued them under the section nine.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: The judge explained on Thursday why the police could keep hold of the former prince's items that had been seized.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: "We ensured the court was presented with all the necessary information and paperwork to inform their decision, following the correct legal processes throughout.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: "We accept the position that the initial court's decision to issue warrants under the specific piece of legislation used was incorrect and therefore these must be legally quashed.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: The next stage in this legal dispute will be a behind-closed-doors hearing over whether the police can still retain material seized from Mountbatten-Windsor's homes under alternative powers designed for situations like this.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: The error that has led to Thames Valley Police accepting the search warrants were unlawful relates to the particular power the judge permitted the force to use when its officers raided the properties.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: Strict legal safeguards on searches bar the police from automatically seizing sensitive material without thinking through in advance the need to take it.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: Examples of that material include advice from a suspect's lawyer or material which does not really belong to them, such as copies of confidential work-related papers from an employer.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: In practice, if the police find such material during a search, they should return it rather than use it in their investigation.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: The category of search warrant that was granted by the court in this instance did not take into account the possibility of such protected material being seized.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: However, the law says police can in fact seize that kind of material - or potentially retain it in the event of an error - providing they pass some extra tests.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: Thames Valley Police must now convince a judge that the material is likely to be of "substantial value" to their investigation into Mountbatten-Windsor and, ultimately, potential evidence to present to a court.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: So while the force has conceded the search warrant was unlawful, a judge will have to decide whether this alternative search power, with its extra safeguards, justifies them keeping and using the material after all.

sentences.text: A panel of wildlife experts drew up a shortlist of 18 mammals, birds, amphibians insects and fish which were put forward to public nominations .

sentences.text: Respondents were invited to select up to six.
sentences.article_title: The wildlife winners set to appear on your banknotes revealed

sentences.text: The European hedgehog (Erinaceus europaeus) was most popular in the mammals category.
sentences.article_title: The wildlife winners set to appear on your banknotes revealed

sentences.article_title: The wildlife winners set to appear on your banknotes revealed

sentences.text: Rainmaker's drones were used over Alaska this year On 23 August, Cooper Freeman had no idea clouds above his head were being filled with a silver compound in order to cause rainfall.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Neither did thousands of other residents in Homer, Alaska, who later discovered a  start-up called Rainmaker conducted an experiment in that region using cloud-seeding technology.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: The company, based in El Segundo California, claims it produced 19 million US gallons of water in the sky in three hours.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: This approach to weather modification, now more than 80-years-old, involves using planes and drones to disperse compounds such as silver iodide into clouds to form ice crystals.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Those crystals eventually become large enough to fall as rain or snow, depending on the temperatures below.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Essentially, cloud seeding speeds up the natural process of water vapor condensing inside of clouds.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Gravity then pulls those crystals to the ground.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: The technology, though, needs ideal climate environments, such as mountainous or cold regions such as Alaska.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Freeman, the Alaska director of the Center for Biological Diversity, isn't just concerned Homer residents weren't widely alerted to these experiments.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: He's sceptical about what was shot into the clouds, and questions how safe it was for both residents and their habitat.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "It doesn't appear that there was any downstream monitoring to verify that this silver iodide didn't impact the environment," he says.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Freeman adds, "Having a company come in to do this seeding isn't going to solve our water woes, and it feels like a distraction from solving the urgent issues related to water conservation." Concerns are mounting about the challenges surrounding water security.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres said in July "our world is using freshwater faster than it can be replenished , external ", which echoes reports noting how the past five years have led to the driest period for global rivers , external in more than three decades.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Cloud-seeding technology may be a drop in the bucket, as it doesn't create rainstorms.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: For example, Rainmaker's 19 million gallons equates to around 0.01 inch of rain across 100 square miles.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Nevertheless, more than 50 countries , external are developing programmes to modify the weather and a surge of start-ups are developing systems to create rain.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: As well developed and promising as this innovative field has become, these businesses continue to face thorny questions on safety and efficacy, leading to novel approaches with both finding the right material to spray into clouds and how they do it.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Augustus Doricko with a Rainmaker drone Augustus Doricko, the founder and CEO of Rainmaker, is quick to answer any questions on the consequences of how his company uses the silver iodide compound.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: It's clear he's been asked about chemical safety many times.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: He says Rainmaker releases this form of silver at 20 grams per flight, distributed across thousands of square kilometres.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Cloud-seeding sessions have to wait for clouds to form to try to coax them into precipitation.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Their drones are outfitted with silver iodide flares, and when lit the burning atomizes the water particles into a small enough size so they can stay suspended in the freezing cloud for hours, eventually turning into crystals and later rain.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Rainmaker operates in states such as Idaho, Utah, Colorado and areas of the Middle East such as Jordan.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: A year later, silver iodide was found to be more effective than dry ice, which quickly turns into useless gas.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: While seeding agents caused more rainfall, they didn't move the needle much.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: In fact, sobering statistics point to how patchy this technology can be in what it pours on the ground.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "With the right conditions, cloud seeding squeeze out about an extra five to 10% of precipitation," says Jon Meyer, an assistant state climatologist with the Utah Climate Center.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: What was encouraging, though, for the cloud-seeding sector was a landmark 2017 study that found how silver iodide worked as expected, one of the first reports to observe cloud seeding in action using radar and precipitation gauges.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: In the past several years, Meyer has been encouraged to see more companies such as Rainmaker bring innovation to an old industry.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "Drones [such as Rainmaker's products] present this new avenue," says Meyer, "and they offer a more targeted nature to these clouds we hope will be responsive." Olivia Li is developing an alternative to silver iodide for cloud seeding What is sprayed into clouds may also be undergoing a major shift.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Recast Systems in San Francisco is experimenting with a type of protein made from amino acids found in the soil, says CEO Olivia Li.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: While still undergoing tests at Texas A&M University, this new seeding agent moves Recast away from silver iodide as the go-to compound.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "It's safe, biodegradable and nucleates ice at a higher efficiency than silver iodide," says Li, whose company currently uses silver iodide to seed clouds in several US states.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Meyer is optimistic this technology's trajectory will only continue to rise.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "We're going to see more demand for these services as so many regions are experiencing water demand," he says, "and they're going to be looking for ways to help bridge that gap." X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Choosing the right moment to harvest can be a make-or-break decision When the first day of the apple harvest rolled around in Washington State last year, the fruit was ripe and the pickers were ready – but the weather had other ideas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It was like 38C… it's not safe for people to work in that heat," recalls Joel Carter at Okanagan Specialty Fruits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We had to stop at 10 o'clock in the morning." He says that artificial intelligence (AI) models that forecast ideal harvest dates, taking into account the weather, would be useful.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "You need to know more than just when your fruit is going to be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: How long do you have to pick it?" he says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "That's where these models are really helpful." Carter's company has more than 1,250 acres of apple orchards in Washington, and the fruit is grown for sliced apple portions – often sold to hotels and schools, for example.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The firm is investing in technology with the hope of maximising productivity.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Even the apples are genetically engineered so that they don't brown easily once cut.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But planning a harvest is tricky.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: New tools that count and analyse fruit on the tree or vine, and predict when crops will ripen, are emerging.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: It matters because prices for fruit, especially high-value berries such as strawberries or blueberries can fluctuate wildly.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Getting the harvest date wrong means you book seasonal workers when you don't actually need them, and risk missing out on the biggest profits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Okanagan Specialty Fruits is already experimenting with cameras from a Canadian firm called Vivid Machines.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The cameras are mounted atop tractors and they scoop up imagery of the apple trees as the tractor trundles by.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: AI identifies buds, flowers or fruit in that footage.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Right now, Vivid is telling us crop estimates and harvest dates," says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He notes that the system is good at picking out very tiny flower buds, which are hard to see at a glance with the naked eye.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But the accuracy of forecasts is noticeably dependent on the quality of historical information fed in to the system, adds Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "This isn't something where an AI can scrape the internet and figure out what's the average [yield] for Granny Smith," he explains.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It's going to be bespoke to your farm." Apples are at least somewhat forgiving – the harvest window for those Granny Smiths is three weeks long, says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: For other fruit, such as berries, you might only have a few days.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "If a strawberry crop is on, you have to harvest it – otherwise your entire crop gets diseased very, very quickly," says Raymond Martin, co-founder and chief operating officer of FruitCast, a UK company that offers harvest forecasts to fruit growers here.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: His firm offers growers crop predictions for strawberries and also raspberries, blackberries, blueberries and tomatoes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We're moving on to grapes next year," adds Martin.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Don't experienced farmers know when their fruit will be ripe, I ask?
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Martin says they generally do – but not necessarily across their entire farm, which might be many acres in size, or have both outdoor and indoor growing areas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We do exactly what the farmers could do but we just do it on a scale that they can't." The system analyses footage of ripening fruit that can be captured by drones, someone walking up and down a field with a smartphone, or a camera mounted on a farm vehicle.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This year has been challenging, notes Martin, with hot weather and severe drought hitting much of the UK .
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This has stressed many fruit plants, putting them into thermal dormancy and slowing down fruit production.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: There's only a small window for picking berries says Raymond Martin The FruitCast model accounts for weather and irrigation conditions in its forecasts.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The company says, "our forecasts land within 10% of actual picked volume one week out (90% accurate) and within 17% three weeks out (83% accurate).
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: We guarantee less than 20% error…" Angus Soft Fruits is one company that has worked with FruitCast.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Yasaman Ghasempour (left) is developing ripeness detection techniques Researchers are also exploring new ways of analysing fruit in intense detail.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Many farmers already use handheld brix meters to gauge the sugar content of their crop.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: These devices work by measuring how much light has changed direction, or refracted, after passing through a liquid – indicating the volume of solids present.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Some such meters use infrared light, meaning there's no need to cut into the fruit to take measurements.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But Yasaman Ghasempour at Princeton University says millimetre waves, high frequency radio waves, can penetrate deeper "They basically respond very well to humidity, water [and sugar]," she says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: She and her students have come up with a millimetre wave-based ripeness detector , external that could be used by farmers – or even customers searching for perfectly ripe fruit in shops.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Her students tried it out at a local market in New Jersey.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "[Staff] there got kind of scared that we were doing something shady," laughs Ghasempour.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Such fine-grained analysis of fruit, if currently unripe, could also help inform forecasts of when it will be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Jing Zhang says new tech has to prove its worth to farmers But while some growers, such as Carter, are interested in trying out new tech, many will wonder whether investing in it is really worthwhile.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Adoption is very complicated," says Jing Zhang at North Carolina State University.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "The grower has to have confidence in the research and whether or not it works." Zhang has been working on a system to automatically count the number of blueberries , external captured in smartphone images of blueberry bushes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The simplest systems need not be expensive.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Kevin Wang at the University of Florida has developed another crop-counting tool that can harvest imagery , external from $100 (£74) drones.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: In the future, such information could feed in to ripeness predictions.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: However, he points out that some farmers might be uneasy about sharing commercially sensitive information about their growing strategies, such as fertiliser and irrigation plans, with third parties and AI models.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Ben Palone is senior director of automation and commercialisation at Western Growers, an association that represents farmers in the western US.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He says harvest forecasts have some potential as "an optimisation tool".
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But farmers will likely continue to rely on human intelligence.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Growers like to have people in the mix to make some of those very critical decisions – especially when it comes to harvests," he says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Albertans will vote on 19 October whether to hold an independence referendum in the future For Alberta independence supporter Keith Wilson, the western Canadian province is in a league of its own.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: With its wealth of rich oil and gas reserves, a significant agricultural sector and a young and skilled workforce, its economy is one to be reckoned with, says Wilson.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: The province will hold a referendum on 19 October, giving residents two options: vote to stay in Canada, or vote to move ahead with a formal binding referendum on independence at a later date.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: The vote, despite not being a cut and dry "stay or leave", still stands to be among the most consequential in recent Canadian history, and a significant test of national unity.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: One key issue has become central to the debate: Would Alberta be richer if it were to become an independent country?
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: The answer for Wilson is yes.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: "Alberta's economy is unique. is fundamentally different than the rest of Canada's - we have the people, the institutions, the infrastructure to excel," he says.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: Alberta separatists have long argued that the province has been short-changed by being part of Canada, and that more of the oil and gas wealth would be kept within its borders instead of being shared with Ottawa, delivering it tens of billions in savings.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: But many disagree with their accounting.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith, who opposes independence, predicts a more sober outcome.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: She says the province could risk paying C$400bn ($283bn; £213bn) in transition costs alone, while bleeding billions more in lost investments and trade due to the political upheaval.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: A report commissioned , external by her government released earlier this month calculated the costs of separation as between C$50bn and C$170bn over five years - and a highly unpredictable outlook over the long term.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: The report cautions that the to-do list for a newly independent Alberta would be long and costly.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: It would have to set up agencies to manage taxes and national security, develop its own constitution, legal and court systems, and pension plans, and negotiate the division of federal assets like national parks and military bases.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: At Canada's biggest rodeo, the starting gun is fired in the fight over Alberta separation Alberta will vote on whether to remain part of Canada.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: Lennie Kaplan, a former finance official in Alberta, says the province would be expected to take on a share of Canada's national debt, among many other fiscal challenges and responsibilities.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: A report on Alberta independence by the CanadaWest Foundation , external , a non-profit Alberta-based think tank, estimates that the province could be stuck with additional debt ranging from C$258bn to C$333bn.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: With a projected hit to Alberta's GDP and the additional costs, the report estimates separation could hit Albertans' bottom line and reduce their disposable income by 5.8% on average.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: "Why do we have to create all this uncertainty that might impact and impair the province's fiscal position going forward?
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: Why wouldn't we just work within Canada to address these issues?" Kaplan asks.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: Opinion polling indicates that around 20% to 25% of Albertans plan to vote in favour of moving ahead with a binding separation referendum, with higher support among younger, rural and conservative voters.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: Behind the separatist push is the belief that Alberta is misunderstood and overlooked by decision-makers in Ottawa.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: For decades, that sentiment fuelled a sense of "western alienation" in the prairie province.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: Once a fringe movement, a number of factors pushed it to the forefront of Alberta politics.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: There was anger over environmental and political pushback that killed proposed pipelines from landlocked Alberta to coastal waters.
sentences.article_title: How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

sentences.text: A decade of Liberal government in Ottawa has also caused frustration in reliably conservative Alberta.

sentences.text: Europe's heatwave has boosted demand for battery storage systems As heatwaves scorched Europe this summer, workers at a US battery company noticed an uptick in demand.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: San Diego-based Unigrid sells a nine kilowatt hour battery for people's homes.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sweltering European homeowners were apparently looking for ways of storing power when it was available from the grid at lower rates.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They could then run air conditioners more cheaply, off the battery, during the worst heat of the day.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We have requests coming from Spain, France, Germany, The Netherlands," says Darren Tan, co-founder and chief executive.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've shipped the first 100 units and [expect to ship] 1,000 before the end of the year." Unigrid's battery is an emerging technology – it's a sodium ion, rather than lithium ion device.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries have got energy storage experts excited because they could end up much cheaper to build and operate than lithium ion.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They're potentially less likely to catch fire and should also work in a wider range of temperatures, even down to lows of minus 40C , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Darren Tan founded Unigrid - a maker of sodium ion batteries But there's a debate over what constitutes the best, and safest, sodium ion battery design.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Plus, more than one , external US company working in this space has floundered in recent years , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: China leads the world in sodium ion battery manufacturing at present so US competitors are going to have to work hard to keep up.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The prize that awaits is the possibility of batteries made in the US with 100% US-sourced materials.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This is unlike lithium ion batteries, where China dominates the materials , external supply chain as well as manufacturing.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: For Tan, China has helped his company get to market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The Unigrid battery currently uses sodium ion cells made there, rather than in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We can switch back and forth and choose what battery we want to work with," says Tan, explaining that, in future, his firm might source cells from the US – though these may come at a different cost.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: There's another consideration.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Unigrid's battery contains chromium-3 in its cathode.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In a battery, electrons flow from cathode to anode , external when charging and in the opposite direction when discharging or providing power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Ivana Hasa, at the Warwick Manufacturing Group, University of Warwick, who has no connection to Unigrid, agrees that it is possible for chromium-3 to form chromium-6 at very high states of charge, though she says this can be mitigated by how voltage is controlled within the battery.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "Safety tests reported on the cell chemistry are very promising," she says of Unigrid's tech.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Tan says concerns around toxicity of the battery's materials are "overblown" and emphasises that Unigrid's battery has passed certification and safety tests for sale in Europe and is currently undergoing such evaluations for the US market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Third-party tests have not been able to get the battery to form chromium-6, he says.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've tried very hard to try and produce it, we've overcharged it as much as we can...
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: We were unsuccessful in generating chromium-6." The choice of cathode material, or how the electrolyte – which separates cathode and anode – is formulated are key details influencing the performance and longevity of sodium ion batteries.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some manufacturers are not using chromium for their cathode but hard carbon instead, or sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate (NFPP).
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In general, confidence around sodium ion batteries' reliability has increased during the last few years, says Prof Dame Grey, meaning they are now finding their way into grid storage applications.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Last December, LFP batteries – a relatively cheap form of lithium ion battery – were trading at $81 per kilowatt hour , external (kWh) whereas Unigrid's sodium ion battery pricing is roughly $100 kWh , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some companies that spoke to the BBC suggested sodium ion might reach as low as $30 per kWh but analysts say significantly lower costs could be many years away , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries are also not as energy dense as lithium ion batteries, meaning they must be slightly bigger and heavier in order to provide the same amount of power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The technology has been improving , external on this front in recent years but, even so, you're not likely to see sodium ion cells in small, energy hungry devices such as smartphones.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Larger energy storage solutions are where most people expect sodium ion to dominate.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Emerald Battery Labs founders (left to right) Aric Stocks, Kjell Schroder, David Bell "We think sodium ion […] is going to make up 80% of the market," says David Bell, co-founder and chief executive of Seattle-based Emerald Battery Labs.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Bell declined to share details of the battery design his firm is working on, though he says Emerald too is currently relying on China-sourced sodium ion cells as they develop their initial product: 12 volt auxiliary batteries for vehicles, currently supplied to unnamed commercial fleets in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We took a look at the market and said 'Hey, no-one's trying to attack this space, let's have Emerald Battery Labs attack it'," says Bell.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The firm's next goal is to develop new anodes for US-produced sodium ion cells.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Another company, Peak Energy, based in California and Colorado, announced a partnership with General Motors (GM) in June.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The pair aim to develop a US supply chain for sodium ion batteries, in order to enable large-scale energy storage for electricity grids.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Peak Energy is also, at present, relying on China-sourced cells for its first installations, but hopes to help GM launch a US-based production facility in Michigan "by the end of 2028", says Cameron Dales, president and co-founder.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "China does not have an insurmountable lead in sodium ion batteries," he says.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Alysm sodium ion batteries are made in the US One reason US companies feel they can compete is because of the electricity demand boom from data centres, which are contributing to rising greenhouse gas emissions in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Data centre-driven demand is also rising in other places around the world, including the UK .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This is an "opportunity" says Drew Buckley, chief executive at ESS Tech, headquartered in Oregon.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: He points out that sodium ion batteries could help distribute renewable energy to data centres.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: And those batteries should be cheaper to run than lithium ion alternatives, since they are not expected to require as much cooling.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: ESS Tech is working with Alsym, another US firm that is planning to ship "hundreds" of megawatt hours' worth of sodium ion batteries – made in the US – by 2027.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Hasa says that it will be "challenging" for companies to establish mass production of sodium ion batteries.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: And she also notes that, while this type of battery is often touted as much safer than lithium ion, they do not come with zero fire risk.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: But if any firms can succeed in this space, they could enable new strategic choices, she adds – helping to avoid wastage of renewable electricity and potentially keeping energy costs low.

sentences.text: "I'm a strong believer in the technology," says Hasa.
