sentences.text: The long nose of the X-59 is designed to dampen the plane's sonic boom There's a weird and wonderful jet flying over the US.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It has the nose of anteater, parts cannibalised from other planes and a cockpit so far back the pilot depends on a camera to see where he's going.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: This contraption, the X-59, might just be the future of air travel.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The X-59's owes its eccentric design to the problem of sonic booms.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The shockwave created by a jet breaking the sound barrier restricted Concorde to flights over the sea and barred it from lucrative routes across the US.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Now Nasa is working around that problem using the X-59's elongated snout to flatten supersonic booms into tolerable bumps in the background.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: On top of its bizarre appearance the X-59 boasts a remarkable lineage.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It's the latest in a series of experimental Nasa aircraft dating back to 1947 and the first plane to break the sound barrier, the Bell X-1.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Peter Coen, a 43-year Nasa veteran who manages the programme, explains the thinking behind 80 years of X-planes.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "Our approach is to pick small goals we aim to prove with flight data and we construct an airframe for that one task." The X-plane philosophy is to "minimise goals, the more goals you have the more expensive it gets." For the X-59 it's about suppressing sonic booms on a budget and nothing else.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: In the case of the X-1, flown through the sound barrier in 1947 by the legendary test pilot Chuck Yeager, Nasa knew a .50 calibre bullet travelled faster than the speed of sound.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: So the stumpy little aircraft was shaped like a bullet with wings added.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: A mere 20 years later the X-15 rocket plane, a cylinder with tiny wings dropped from a B-52 bomber, flew to 6.7 times the speed of sound (4,520 mph) and the edge of space, paving the way for heat-resistant materials vital to the Space Shuttle.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: In 1947 the Bell X-1 was the first plane to break the sound barrier Nasa will fly the X-59 in conjunction with community surveys to assess what people think when a supersonic boom is bent by the planes stretched nose and hushed up.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "We want to figure out what level of boom is acceptable to people on a regular basis," says Coen, who reckons his machine will sound "like a car door being closed across the street" when it flies past Mach 1, around 660mph at airline cruising altitude.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: With its cockpit and ejector seat taken from a T-38 training jet, its landing gear from an F-16 fighter and engine courtesy of the F-18 this jigsaw of an aircraft was assembled by Lockheed Martin for Nasa.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: A camera feeding a screen in front of the pilot relies on instantaneous computer processing to get round the lack of forward vision.

sentences.text: She largely left the issue – and the Conservative policy to withdraw from the European Convention on Human Rights, as Reform also advocates - to her shadow home secretary Chris Philp who spoke before her.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Tories united behind Badenoch - but party still needs to win over voters

sentences.text: Instead, Badenoch grounded this speech in the big picture tussle to be trusted between Labour and the Conservatives – and in particular who was better placed to deliver a growing economy.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Tories united behind Badenoch - but party still needs to win over voters

sentences.text: In tone, language and public enthusiasm for the argument, Badenoch and Andy Burnham are quite the contrast with their immediate predecessors Rishi Sunak and Sir Keir Starmer.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Tories united behind Badenoch - but party still needs to win over voters

sentences.text: Badenoch and Burnham both look like they are enjoying themselves on the stage, and are both enthusiastic purveyors of the core of what are their very different worldviews.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Tories united behind Badenoch - but party still needs to win over voters

sentences.text: Badenoch acknowledged this with what she called the "battle for the soul of this nation" in the opening minute or so of her address.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Tories united behind Badenoch - but party still needs to win over voters

sentences.text: It is a trailer for the debate to come this autumn and beyond.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Tories united behind Badenoch - but party still needs to win over voters

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: The big test facing Kemi Badenoch after her conference speech The Conservatives feel chipper and are united.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Tories united behind Badenoch - but party still needs to win over voters

sentences.text: But while both of these things are better than the alternative for any party leader, they are not the same as being popular.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Tories united behind Badenoch - but party still needs to win over voters

sentences.text: And, as Kemi Badenoch acknowledged, they are not there on that score yet, by a long chalk, with opinion polls suggesting they are more unpopular than when they were annihilated at the last general election.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Tories united behind Badenoch - but party still needs to win over voters

sentences.text: The numbers, for them, are dire.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Tories united behind Badenoch - but party still needs to win over voters

sentences.text: Just not as bad, relatively speaking, as they were.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Tories united behind Badenoch - but party still needs to win over voters

sentences.text: But they hope things are looking up for them: Reform has had a bruising few months, and Labour, they believe, are leaning to the Left, trying to lure Green and Liberal Democrat supporters towards them.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Tories united behind Badenoch - but party still needs to win over voters

sentences.text: Can the Conservatives also lure recent Lib Dem supporters in the south of England with talk of help with childcare costs whatever your income , not hiking the council tax of very expensive homes and this inheritance tax plan?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Tories united behind Badenoch - but party still needs to win over voters

sentences.text: This, Tories hope, there are now gaps in the political market they can exploit.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Tories united behind Badenoch - but party still needs to win over voters

sentences.text: They crave catching and overtaking Reform in the polls, in the hope that after that there is a tipping point allowing them to credibly claim they are the most viable alternative to a Labour or Labour-led future government.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Tories united behind Badenoch - but party still needs to win over voters

sentences.text: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has announced she will overhaul inheritance tax if her party wins the next general election.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: She told the Conservatives' annual conference that "nobody will ever pay inheritance tax on their family home" and couples will be able to leave an additional £1m tax free.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: Tax experts say the party's £6bn per year estimate of the cost of the plan is reasonable, but warn the policy would primarily benefit wealthier households and could discourage older people from moving to smaller homes.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: BBC Verify has looked into the details of the policy.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: Under the current system, inheritance tax of 40% is paid when someone's estate - the total value of their money and property - exceeds £325,000.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: Anything under this amount is not taxed.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: And, when a person dies, they can currently transfer this tax-free allowance to a surviving spouse or civil partner which increases the combined threshold for a couple to £650,000.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: On top of this individuals can get an additional transferable allowance for a family home of £175,000 each when it is left to children or other direct descendants.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: So at present most married couples can potentially leave £1m without paying inheritance tax.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The Conservative plan would increase the £325,000 threshold - the point at which you start paying the tax - to £500,000 and fully exempt a family home from inheritance tax.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: At the moment an estate with a £2m house could be liable for £400,000 in inheritance tax.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: That would reduce to zero under the Conservatives.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: Official figures show that in 2024-25 around 30,400 deaths in the UK left estates which were liable for inheritance tax.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: This was around 5% of all UK deaths in that year.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: But the number of estates paying inheritance tax is set to rise, due to the increasing value of inherited wealth being passed on and the threshold having been frozen.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) has estimated that by 2032-33 around 12% of people will have inheritance tax due either on their own death or that of their spouse or civil partner.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: Citing analysis by the consultancy Oxford Economics, the Conservatives say the number of estates paying the tax will rise to 52,100 in 2029-30.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The Conservatives estimate their reforms would reduce the number of affected estates in 2030 to 22,000.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: Official data shows higher value estates pay the majority of the inheritance tax collected.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The IFS has estimated that if inheritance tax were to be entirely scrapped, which Badenoch has identified as a longer term aspiration, the wealthiest 1% of estates - those worth £2.1m or more - would get half of the benefit of the tax reduction.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: And one long-standing criticism of inheritance tax is that the wealthy use legal ways to avoid paying it like putting their assets into family trusts to reduce the amount of inheritance tax ultimately due from their estates when they die.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: In 2023-24, estates with a valuation of £10m only paid an average effective inheritance tax rate of 18%, according to estimates from HM Revenue and Customs.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: Responding to Wednesday's conference announcement, the IFS said: "The biggest beneficiaries would be those with the highest wealth and the most valuable homes – and their descendants.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: "This is a very well-off group, mainly living in London and the South-East of England." The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), the official forecaster, estimates inheritance tax will raise £9.5bn in 2026-27 - equivalent to around 0.3% of GDP.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The OBR projects this will rise to £14.5bn in 2030-31 or 0.4% of GDP.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The Conservatives estimate their plan would cost £6bn a year in 2029-30, based on Oxford Economics' analysis.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The party says it has identified £71bn in annual savings including £36bn a year from welfare cuts.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: Prof Andy Summers, director of the Centre for the Analysis of Taxation, told BBC Verify this was "just about about the worst possible way to deliver an inheritance tax cut".
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: "Exempting the family home however much it's worth will just encourage older people to concentrate their savings in their home, prevent downsizing, and so further gum up the housing market," he said.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The Conservatives argue in their press release accompanying the policy announcement that inheritance taxes are "bad for growth".
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: But analysis by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development suggests inheritance taxes in general are less damaging to economic growth than taxes on income from work.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The Tories are in an upbeat mood at their annual conference Political party conferences can be weird events - where positive thinking and hopeful rhetoric can crowd out reality.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: If you spend enough time drinking and socialising with like-minded people anything can seem possible.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: That could be one explanation for the upbeat mood of this year's Conservative gathering in Birmingham.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: On the face of it, the party has made little progress since it was emphatically ejected from power in 2024.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: If an election was held tomorrow, it would do even worse than it did back then, according to some polls.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: Yet senior figures, including leader Kemi Badenoch, are talking about winning the next general election outright and forming a government.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: One reason for their optimism is that they appear to have seen off, for now, the threat of being destroyed or swallowed up by Reform UK - a prospect which hung over last year's conference amid swirling rumours of defections and speculation about deals with Nigel Farage.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: Another is Badenoch herself, who appears to have made a positive impression on the public.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: In particular, her punchy performances at Prime Minister's Questions have made a strong impression, earning plaudits such as "intelligent", "professional" and "principled" from those who have seen her in action, according to Tryl.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: But like Burnham, Badenoch's personal popularity has yet to transfer to her party, he added, with the Tories being seen as "outdated" and "divided".
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: It was not all gloom – in contrast to his presentation at last year's Tory conference –  and there were "signs of recovery", Tryl said, with a large pool of voters out there who might consider voting Tory, under the right circumstances.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: Conservatives freely admit the problem they have got is that voters don't trust them to deliver on any of their promises, when they had 14 years in government to do something about the problems they now say are so pressing.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: "Of course, Kemi's ahead of us, we know that," Conservative chairman Kevin Hollinrake told the More in Common meeting.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: "Because people do trust Kemi and they don't trust us, that's how I would put it in a nutshell.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: "But we are building on that." Badenoch answers the trust question by saying that the party is under new management now.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: She has ditched some of the "culture war" rhetoric and is focusing hard on the economy, and setting out her guiding principles, which amount to a return to old-school Conservatism.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: She is not saying that the party could win an election outright if it was held now, arguing that no one could.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: But she has ruled out governing with Reform UK in a hung parliament, telling the BBC she would rather hold another election .
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: Hollinrake sounded a cautious note at the More In Common fringe.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: "We are not where we need to be right now.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: We don't want an election right now, ideally.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: Ideally, it would come way down the track." But deputy leader Alex Burghart was quick to stress that the party is making every effort to ensure it is ready for a snap election.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: "We are preparing for an election now," he told the meeting.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: But they still trail Reform by four or five points in the polls and are as much as nine points behind Labour.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: The next challenge for the party, former Scottish Conservative leader Baroness Ruth Davidson said, was to become one of the "top two".
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: At that point, voters who want to see the back of Labour would start moving to the Tories in serious numbers, she argued.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: Tactical voting could prove crucial at the next election, whenever it comes, with many people voting to keep parties out of power rather than for who they want to win.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: The Tories think they have a strong hand here too.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: "For the first time in history, the Conservative Party is now the least hated political party in the country," declared Hollinrake, to laughter and applause.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: "When it comes to tactical voting, that's really important." Not the most inspiring rallying cry you will hear at a party conference, perhaps, but it is grounded in reality.
sentences.article_title: Why Tories are talking about winning the next election

sentences.text: There is a risk of people being over-diagnosed with ADHD and autism, an official review in England has found.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Experts said a rise in diagnoses over the past 25 years meant cases now appear to be outstripping the expected number in the population for some younger age groups.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: The review called for tougher regulation of private firms offering assessments for the NHS, saying they had concerns about quality and consistency, and a ban on advertising.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: It concluded economic uncertainty combined with social media was driving an increase in mental health problems among young people and said there needed to be better support in place for all conditions.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: The review - led by leading doctors in the field - was ordered 10 months ago by Wes Streeting after the then-health secretary claimed in an interview that young people were over-diagnosed and "written off".
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: It looked at people of all ages, but particularly focused on young people and children who have the highest rates of diagnoses.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: It is likely to feed into government policies on everything from NHS services and benefits to support for young people who are not in education, employment or training.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: The experts said too often diagnoses of mental health problems and ADHD and autism were ending up as labels that defined people by their "difficulties rather than their strengths and potential", harming their prospects at school, in work and in relationships.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Children diagnosed with autism and ADHD before the age of 17 are around four times more likely to end up not in education, employment or training between 16 and 24.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: With better support after diagnosis, they could be helped to live more fulfilling lives, the review said.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Alongside access to therapies, this should also include support for mental health – significant numbers also struggle with conditions such as depression.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: But the review found people were also being harmed by long waits for diagnosis for mental health and ADHD and autism.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: The Watsons are just one family who have experience of this.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Ryan and his wife knew there was something different with their son Atlas when he was around 12 to 18 months old and missing development milestones.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: But it took three years to get an autism assessment.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: As time passed, his needs became increasingly clear.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Now nearly seven, Atlas is non-verbal, still wears nappies and relies on others for all aspects of daily care.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Despite this, Ryan said there was no fast-track route for children with the most complex needs.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: "You basically go on the list and wait however long until you get to the top." The wait left the family racing against time to secure support before Atlas started school.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Ryan and his wife feared he would be placed in a mainstream school.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: "We were terrified," Ryan says.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: "Anyone who has a child like Atlas will have the same panic that they'll start in a mainstream school where it's not safe." The strain was immense.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: "It was like I had two jobs," Ryan says.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: "I was going to work and then coming home and dealing with these things." Atlas was eventually diagnosed only months before starting school.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: This could include adjustments being made at school or in workplaces and lifestyle support, such as help to improve sleep or address anxiety, it said.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Too often, access to help requires a diagnosis, with experts highlighting changes in 2014 that required parents to get a diagnosis of autism and ADHD to qualify their children for extra support in schools.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Review chair Prof Peter Fonagy said it was clear the system was "under immense strain" and it was time to get away from diagnosis being a "very narrow pathway" to finding support.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: It said there was a risk society was now moving from an era of under-diagnosis to over-diagnosis or mis-diagnosis, pointing to data showing more than 4% of children aged six to 17 were now diagnosed with autism, well above the 1-2% that studies suggest is the true level.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: But it said because some of these figures date back nearly a decade it was not possible to be absolutely certain or conclude over-diagnosis was currently occurring at scale.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: And there are some age groups where these neurological conditions are still being under-diagnosed – and that should not be over-looked either, it added.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: Mel Merritt, of the National Autistic Society, said the report shows that successive governments "have failed autistic people".
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: "The harm and distress autistic people are facing is real and widespread and there is a desperate need to build a system that supports the needs of autistic people." Abigail Ampofo, of charity YoungMinds, said: "For years, young people have told us they feel blamed for their mental health or accused of making it up.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: We hope this review goes some way to show them their distress is not their fault and the systems around them are failing." But she said that would require major reform.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: The government welcomed the publication of the report and said it would be setting out a new model of providing support in its forthcoming mental health strategy, which is expected before the end of the year, and also promised to introduce tougher regulation of ADHD and autism assessments.
sentences.article_title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review

sentences.text: The NHS in England experienced its busiest September on record There are "ominous signs" that winter pressures are already affecting the NHS in England, according to senior health leaders.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: The warning comes as new data reveals the waiting list for routine hospital treatment in England rose for the second month in a row.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: An estimated 7.37 million treatments were waiting to be carried out at the end of August, relating to 6.24 million patients.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: The numbers are the highest since October 2025 and have raised questions over whether the NHS will meet a government target of treating 92% of patients within 18 weeks by 2029.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: The rise in waiting lists comes despite the NHS in England delivering what were described as record levels of planned, elective care over the summer, while demand for services also reached its highest level ever.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: A record 4.7 million planned treatments, procedures and appointments occurred across June, July and August – more than in any previous summer.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: But both A&Es and ambulance services also saw a record number of patients for the month of September.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: NHS England's national medical director, Professor Frankie Swords, warned that despite the progress delivered by frontline teams, winter pressure was already building.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: "Staff are already seeing the ominous early signs of pressure, with more patients coming to A&E with flu and other respiratory viruses than usual for this time of year, and unfortunately many people are still waiting longer than we would like them to," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: Health and Social Care Secretary, Yvette Cooper said the NHS has been dealing with summer pressures as well as winter pressures.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: "It is a huge tribute to doctors, nurses and staff across the NHS that alongside dealing with unprecedented levels of A&E attendances and ambulance call-outs, they also managed to deliver record numbers of elective appointments, procedures and treatments.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: "Step by step, our NHS has been increasing its delivery and performance, making a real difference to patients' lives even as demand is growing.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: That 18-week target hasn't been hit for a decade.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: A separate analysis by the Health Foundation think-tank said progress on cutting waiting times had stalled over the past year, with referrals on to the waiting list rising at a much quicker rate than the number of patients being treated.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: More patients, including children, have been arriving at A&E departments with flu and other respiratory viruses.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: The number of patients seen within four hours in A&Es last month fell to 74.4%,  down from 75.0% in August.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: The number of people waiting more than 12 hours in A&E departments from a decision to admit to actually being admitted – what is known as "corridor care" – stood at 50,582 in September, up from 44,951 in August.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: That has alarmed Dr Vicky Price, president of the Society for Acute Medicine.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: "A 13% year-on-year rise in 12-hour emergency department waits as winter approaches should set alarm bells ringing.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: "More than 50,000 patients waited over 12 hours from the decision to admit to admission in September - 1,686 people every day.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: "These are not just numbers.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: "They represent vulnerable people who are waiting far too long for a bed and staff trying to deliver safe care in overcrowded emergency departments." The government says the 18-week mark could still be achieved, saying it was investing in NHS buildings and equipment to make services more productive.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: It also pointed to disruption to care that was caused by the strikes by resident doctors, a dispute which has now been settled.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: But the strain that services are feeling in September, before winter has even really got going, will be a cause for concern among NHS leaders and their political bosses alike.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: Now NHS needs to change' When Poppy Russell died shortly after birth, her parents were left bereft.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: What followed made matters harder to bear - her mother was blamed for the death.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: An inquest would later conclude that Poppy's death was preventable.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: But instead of walking away from the trust that had failed them, Neil and Katie Russell are now working with it to bring compassionate care back into the NHS.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: "We could have very easily been consumed by hate and anger and rage at what happened – and those feelings are still there," said Katie.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: "But if no change comes from what happened to Poppy, then what's the point?" Neil and Katie Russell are working with the hospital where their daughter died Poppy Russell died in April 2021 at the Princess Royal Hospital in Telford.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: She was just 12 hours old.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: During her pregnancy her mother told midwives that she had tokophobia, a fear of natural birth and wanted a caesarean section.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: Katie said she was repeatedly told however that she "couldn't just ask for a c-section." When she went into labour, Katie was induced and then "we were left in a room for long periods of time where I had no care," she explained.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: "Finally, when we got into the labour suite, I wasn't monitored appropriately and they missed signs that Poppy was in distress." In a bitter irony, Poppy had to be delivered by emergency caesarean.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: By then however, she had developed a hypoxic brain injury and died later the same day.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: An inquest into her death found that had Poppy been born an hour earlier, she would have survived .
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: The Shrewsbury and Telford NHS Trust (SaTH), which ran the hospital, subsequently blamed Katie for her daughter's death.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: They said she had refused foetal monitoring; the inquest concluded that was untrue.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: "The trust left us in an appalling position," said Neil Russell.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: "Not only were they found to have neglected our care, but in the months and years following, we uncovered that members of staff had tried to cover it up.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: In March 2024, the couple had a meeting with the trust to discuss all that had happened.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: From the discussions, Neil and Katie decided they needed to honour Poppy.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: "The first conversations about Poppy's Promise were about being human," said Neil, 45.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: It's someone coming into a room holding your hand, someone acknowledging the fact that this is difficult for you," said Katie.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: Even in the midst of her poor care at the time of her daughter's death, Katie, 41, vividly remembers one midwife who showed some compassion.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: "She came in and said, 'how are you doing?
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: I just want to hug you.' "She sat with me and she cried with me and she said, 'this should never have happened,' and that will always stay with me because it's exactly what I needed at that point." At the time of Poppy's death, SaTH was in the middle of a large maternity inquiry.
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: The review found that 201 babies and nine mothers might have survived with better care .
sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.article_title: 'I was blamed for my baby's death, now NHS needs to change'

sentences.text: Eleanor Tobin (right) says she's no stranger to hang-xiety after a night out You wake up.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: Then comes the second wave: a low, gnawing horror at what you might have done.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: You scroll back through last night's messages, certain you said something wrong.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: You replay conversations worried you offended someone, embarrassed yourself, or both.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: "It's that nagging feeling of dread," says 25-year old Eleanor Tobin who works in marketing and events in London.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: "If the day starts with me doing a checklist of my things - panically checking I have my bag, my phone - I know the anxiety is going to seep into everything I do beyond just reliving the night before." This is hang-xiety,  a name coined in social slang a decade ago, for the anxiety that can accompany a hangover.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: "Alcohol affects the body in many ways - the brain, sleep, hormones and nervous system - that all help explain why a night out drinking can be followed by an excessively anxious morning," says Celia Morgan, professor of psychopharmacology at the University of Exeter.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Yes, hang-xiety is a real thing Alcohol affects two chemical messengers in the brain: GABA and glutamate.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: GABA acts a little like the brain's braking system, reducing nerve-cell activity.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: Glutamate is involved in excitation and alertness.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: Alcohol enhances the effects of GABA and suppresses some glutamate activity, helping to produce that familiar feeling of relaxation and lowered inhibitions.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: But the brain is constantly trying to restore balance.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: As alcohol wears off, the nervous system can swing towards greater alertness and arousal.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: This can trigger anxiety.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: "Everything is always 100% worse in my mind when you have a hangover than in reality," says Tobin.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: A 2023 study of over 5,000 students from the UK and the Netherlands, concluded that 18.3% reported symptoms of anxiety when hungover.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: For the 25-year-old, it can lead to an anxious spiral at the end of a weekend Studies also suggest that not everyone gets hang-xiety, and the level of anxiety does not neatly correlate with how much you drink the night before.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: Existing psychological characteristics – and potentially genetics – appear to play a part.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: In 2019 researchers at the University of Exeter studied this in 97 social drinkers.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: Those who drank reported a spike in anxiety the following day compared with a control group who stayed sober.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: The effect was strongest in people who had scored highly for shyness before drinking.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: Morgan's research found that shy drinkers often felt less anxious during the evening itself.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: Alcohol was doing exactly what they hoped, quieting social nerves, but the rebound came the next day.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: "Shy people were hit even harder the next morning, with hugely elevated anxiety markers, especially when compared with those that weren't naturally shy," says Morgan.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: There is a psychological layer, too.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: Innocuous moments get reinterpreted as embarrassing.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: A perfectly normal joke becomes, in the retelling inside your own head, a terrible mistake.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: The anxious spiral can outlast the physical symptoms, because it feeds on itself: worry disrupts thinking, and disrupted thinking produces more worry.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: If Tobin has been out Friday and Saturday night, by Sunday that spiral can become overwhelming.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: "Suddenly taking the underground can feel like a challenge - normal stuff feels hard when you got a really bad case of the 'Sunday scaries' triggered by two hangovers in a row," she says.

sentences.text: Drinking alcohol can affect sleep as well as trigger severe anxiety the next day You may have fallen asleep quickly after drinking, but that doesn't mean you've had a good night's sleep, researchers warn.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: Alcohol disrupts sleep, including the pattern of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, which is important for emotional regulation.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: "Light and broken sleep means you wake feeling on edge," says Dr Alanna Hare, President of the British Sleep Society.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: "Even if you have eight hours in bed, you haven't had a proper night's sleep, and a tired brain is more reactive to worry." The advice from researchers is unglamorous but consistent.

sentences.text: Moderating alcohol intake matters more than any remedy taken afterwards.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: Drinking water between alcoholic drinks can help, so can eating during your night out.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: Alcohol Change UK director Andrew Misell says it's important not to reach for alcohol to manage or mask stress.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: "Alcohol turns into a depressant and can exacerbate all sorts of problems with our physical and mental health," he says, advising people to see their GP if they are struggling with the spiral.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: Talking to a close friend can also be a good starting point.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: And perhaps the most useful trick if you are suffering with hang-xiety is to reframe the thoughts.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: Recognising hang-xiety as a temporary state, rather than proof that something has gone horribly wrong socially, can blunt its power.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: The catastrophe it points to usually isn't.
sentences.article_title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?

sentences.text: So the next time the Sunday morning spiral sets in, remember it may simply be your brain and body trying to regain balance after alcohol.

sentences.text: Oxevision uses infrared sensors and cameras to monitor patients while they are in their bedrooms Ten mental health trusts have been reported to the health regulator after problems with patient consent procedures when monitoring patients using camera technology.

sentences.text: The issue emerged during the latest hearings of the Lampard Inquiry, which is examining the deaths of more than 2,000 people who spent time in mental health units in Essex between 2000 and the end of 2023.

sentences.text: The infrared technology is used in patients' bedrooms and can monitor breathing and pulse without staff having to enter the room.

sentences.text: The Nobel Committee made the announcement at the Karolinska Institute, Sweden US psychiatrist and neurologist Karl Deisseroth and his German colleagues Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel have been awarded this year's Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their work in the field of optogenetics.

sentences.text: Their research has helped scientists learn more about the inner workings of the brain, to better understand how the human mind works.
sentences.article_title: Nobel Prize awarded for revealing inner workings of the brain

sentences.text: The Nobel Committee , external praised the trio for laying the foundation of a new era in neuroscience by revealing how to switch on and off neural circuits behind "specific memories, feelings, and behaviours relevant for neurological and psychiatric disorders".
sentences.article_title: Nobel Prize awarded for revealing inner workings of the brain

sentences.text: In clinical medicine, researchers are using the method to try to restore sight in people with visual impairment .

sentences.text: "Optogenetics has fundamentally altered our understanding of the brain," the Nobel Assembly said.
sentences.article_title: Nobel Prize awarded for revealing inner workings of the brain

sentences.text: "Every day brings new discoveries, helping to solve one of humanity's great mysteries: how our incredible brain works." The winners said it was "absolutely wonderful" to get the award, and that it was an honour to share the accolade with friends.
sentences.article_title: Nobel Prize awarded for revealing inner workings of the brain

sentences.text: The three men will also share the £900,000 (12 million Swedish kronor) prize money.
sentences.article_title: Nobel Prize awarded for revealing inner workings of the brain

sentences.text: Per Svenningsson, chair of the Nobel Committee for Physiology or Medicine, explained: "Optogenetics provides opportunities for mapping the brain in a way that we could once only dream of." Before, the inner workings behind feelings, behaviours and bodily functions were more of a mystery to scientists.

sentences.text: Optogenetics is a way to illuminate brain pathways, using a special protein borrowed from algae that scientists use to control cell electrical activity using light.
sentences.article_title: Nobel Prize awarded for revealing inner workings of the brain

sentences.text: In the early 2000s, Hegemann and Nagel discovered channelrhodopsin, the algal protein with unique properties.
sentences.article_title: Nobel Prize awarded for revealing inner workings of the brain

sentences.text: Have you ever slept next to a snoring partner and woken up feeling stressed, unfocused or forgetful the next day?
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: As snoring is relatively common, it is often left untreated and dismissed as a harmless irritation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But according to experts, sleeping next to a snorer could be impacting your health.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Snoring is caused by the vibration of the soft tissues in our upper airways during sleep, explains Dr Clare Simon, a dentist with a special interest in dental sleep medicine.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: About 40% of the UK adult population snores, with the issue affecting more men than women, says the British Snoring and Sleep Apnoea Association (BSSAA).
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: And 75% of people with a snoring partner say they have had their sleep impacted, according to a US survey by the Sleep Foundation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know about the impact on partners - and what you can do about it.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Prof Ama Johal, a consultant orthodontist and sleep expert at Aerox Health, explains that the partner of a snorer can become "so impacted upon that it's almost a last-ditch effort on their part to get up and go sleep in a separate room because they have to sleep".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: He adds: "As humans we physically can't function without that necessity." Prof Ama Johal says many couples put up with the negative effects snoring for too long During the night, we cycle through different stages of sleep in repeating patterns, usually every 90 minutes.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: The deeper stages of this cycle are important for physical restoration.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If sleep is frequently disrupted, you may spend less time in the restorative stages, meaning you can wake up feeling tired, even if you've spent a lot of time in bed, the BSSAA explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Your brain processes and stores information from the day during sleep.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Fragmented sleep - which can happen if you're waking up due to a snoring partner - can interrupt this process, impacting your focus and memory.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Disrupted sleep can also impact hormone regulation, which affects your energy levels and motivation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Sleep also plays a role in regulating the brain systems involved in stress and emotional response.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: When it is disrupted, these systems can become less balanced, which may make you feel more irritable and less able to cope with stress.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: This is something Meg Warren, 29, experienced when her former partner's snoring would keep her up.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says: "Without fail, after a snoring-induced wake up I would feel on incredibly high alert." Meg, a charity media officer, would prod him throughout the night and try to coax him from his back to his side.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says she would wake up "feeling groggy and dazed, sometimes so much so that it would feel like a hangover".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Meg Warren felt 'groggy and dazed' after a night of little sleep due to her former partner's snoring Anna-Louise Dearden, a 52-year-old journalist, says she sometimes sleeps in a separate room from her partner due to his snoring.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Having this option allows her to prioritise getting enough rest when the snoring is particularly bad.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: There are things that can be done, say both Simon and Johal.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But first, it is important to distinguish whether your partner is simply snoring, or whether they have sleep apnoea.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: "What you don't want to do is simply make someone quieter at night while potentially missing an underlying sleep-related breathing disorder," Simon says.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Signs of sleep apnoea, a disorder that causes a person's breathing to repeatedly stop and start during sleep, include pauses in breathing, choking at night, waking frequently, and suffering from morning headaches.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If this is what you are dealing with, you could be recommended a Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) machine, or even surgical treatment in some cases, Simon explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: For simple snoring, Simon said that lifestyle changes can make a difference, such as losing weight, stopping smoking, reducing alcohol intake before bed, or changing your sleeping position - such as laying on your side rather than your back.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: You can also suggest to your partner that they see a GP, who will be able to advise further or refer you to a specialist.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: An expert might suggest treating nasal obstruction or allergies, if this is what is causing snoring, or wearing a custom mouthguard to gently push the lower jaw forward and keep the airway open.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Johal says too many couples put up with snoring "for too long", which impacts their relationships and wellbeing.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: "The key thing is that there is help out there, it's just tapping into it." How sleep tracking can make your sleep worse The hidden cost of the night shift and how to sleep it off

sentences.text: Mindy says people often presume she is straight because of her age As a 75-year-old lesbian, Mindy Meleyal has lived through every major milestone in the modern LGBT rights movement, from the start of decriminalisation in 1967 to the first same-sex marriages in 2014.

sentences.text: The report, from the Centre for Ageing Better, says without specialist support, this growing demographic could be forced "back into the closet" when accessing care, warning they may even delay getting the care they need because of concerns about homophobia.

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Sarah Mackay, known as @fitwsarah online, says her energy levels change through her cycle A woman points to a colour-coded grid dividing the menstrual cycle into four phases, each paired with a different list of exercises.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "When you're bleeding, you want to be doing steady-pace jogging, Pilates, barre, walking, resting," she tells viewers.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This is one of thousands of videos on TikTok and Instagram suggesting that people change their workouts depending on where they are in their menstrual cycles - something known as 'cycle-syncing'.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: So-called cycle-syncing workout plans have surged in popularity online, with Google searches for the term rising 740% since 2022 and more than 55,000 TikTok videos now using the #cyclesyncing hashtag.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Most of the advice is shared by fitness and wellness creators rather than medical or research experts.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Kelly McNulty, a researcher at Leeds Beckett University specialising in menstrual cycles and exercise, says there is evidence that some women experience changes in symptoms, energy or perceived strength across their cycle.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But that is different from evidence that all women should train in a particular way at a particular point, she tells the BBC, adding that these videos are "a trend based on marketing rather than any kind of research or evidence".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "There isn't any research to support that kind of phase-based prescription," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This video can not be played Should you sync your exercise routine with your period?
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: A key issue is that menstrual cycles are highly individual, McNulty adds - they can differ between women, and one woman's experience can also change from one cycle to the next.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: That makes the blanket advice often found on social media difficult to apply, she explains.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Many cycle-tracking apps and programmes are also designed around relatively regular menstrual cycles that are 21 to 35 days, which can make their recommendations less applicable to people with irregular periods, or those using hormonal contraception.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She doesn't follow a prescriptive plan, she says, but instead makes changes intuitively.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my luteal phase I'll try and ease off in the training," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my follicular phase, I'm so energised, I feel like I can lift so much heavier.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: I like to try and get my long runs in." Burgoyne also welcomes the growing attention on women's health, and says that exercise and nutrition research has historically focused heavily on male bodies, with findings then often applied to women.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Sarah says she has sometimes hit personal records while on her period Fitness creator Sarah Mackay, known as @liftwsarah on Instagram and TikTok, has also noticed her energy, motivation, cramps and mood change through the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But she deliberately avoids strict plans because, she says, "there are too many variables at play".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Some online plans advise women to avoid intense training during their period, she says, yet she has sometimes hit personal records while menstruating.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "The problem is not that the menstrual cycle is irrelevant," she says, but that "not everything is predictable".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Dr Faye Bate, a trained medical doctor and women's health expert, is also wary of advice suggesting all women should train differently according to their menstrual phase.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "A one-size-fits-all model of 'you should be exercising this way in this phase and a different way in a different phase' shouldn't be advice that applies to all women," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She is concerned that repeatedly telling women they are likely to be weaker or less capable at particular points in their cycle could create a "nocebo" effect - where negative expectations themselves influence how someone feels or performs.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty tells the BBC that routinely easing off resistance training could also limit progress.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Strength training is particularly important for women, who face a higher risk of osteoporosis later in life.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: While cycle-syncing itself may not be backed by strong evidence, the experts we spoke to did suggest being "cycle-aware".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty says tracking your cycle can be a useful way to understand your own patterns, while Dr Bate also encourages women to become more familiar with how they feel at different points in the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Both welcome the fact that menstrual health is being discussed more openly, but say the focus should be on individual experience, rather than rigid, phase-based rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In practice, that might mean having painkillers ready before your period, taking a rest day when symptoms are worse, or easing off a workout if you feel unusually fatigued.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: For Dr Bate, "the most important part is tuning in to how you feel".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In other words, use your cycle as information rather than a set of rules.

sentences.text: Sleep scores, magnesium, white noise machines - what was once the simple act of sleeping has become a minefield.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Trying to optimise sleep in this way is called "sleepmaxxing".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Take it too far, and you could end up with "orthosomnia" - the clinical term for an obsession with achieving perfect sleep.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: While it's not formally recognised as a condition in the UK, doctors tell the BBC they've noticed signs of orthosomnia in their patients, with some bringing their sleep tracker data into appointments convinced, wrongly, that they have a sleep disorder.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: That fixation is actually making people's sleep worse, they warn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: So how and why did sleep become so complicated?
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: And if sleepmaxxing isn't the answer, what is the elusive secret to a good night's sleep?
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The first commercial fitness tracker to incorporate sleep analysis was the Fitbit Classic in 2009.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Since then, many others - including Garmin, Whoop and Apple - have integrated sleep trackers into wrist-worn devices, as have smart rings such as Oura, Ultrahuman and RingConn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: These devices vary, but in general they all provide users with a report of their night, broken down by sleep stages - time awake, light sleep, deep sleep, and REM (rapid eye movement).
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Many also give users a "sleep score".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: But the concept of a sleep score is "completely made up", according to Dr Alanna Hare, consultant of sleep medicine at the Royal Brompton Hospital in London.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "There's nothing recognised in sleep science that is a 'sleep score'," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "That's just been created by manufacturers." This video can not be played How sleep-tracking can make your sleep worse Hare says she's noticed trackers causing anxiety among her patients.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I've noticed more patients coming to me with data from various trackers, with lots of questions about sleep that... is probably contributing to their sleep difficulties," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Even though some have had medical tests with reassuring results, this hasn't allayed their fears, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "It's great that there's more focus on sleep as part of wellness," she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "But sleep just does not respond well to attempts to perfect it." One proposed lawsuit against Oura, filed last month in San Francisco, alleges that Oura rings are unable to accurately measure sleep quality and sleep stages, and instead rely on AI-generated estimates that have "a coin flip's chance of being correct".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: In response, Oura told the BBC that it "stand[s] behind our science, research and accuracy claims".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "We're committed to clearly communicating what Oura measures, what it estimates, and how members should use that information," the company added.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Studies also show sleep trackers can affect how you function during the day, even if they're not accurate.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: In one study , external from the University of Oxford, participants were given sleep trackers which assigned them a sleep score.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The scores were randomised, however, and had no relation to how the participants had actually slept.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The next day participants rated their mood, fatigue levels and alertness, before tests checking their focus and reaction times.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Researchers found that the people told they'd slept badly reported feeling more fatigued, and were less mentally alert - even though the sleep scores were all fake.

sentences.text: This is something Jess Hill says she noticed in herself after getting a Garmin watch several years ago.

sentences.text: "I started to rely on the watch as my Bible for whether I slept well or not," the 32-year-old HR professional from London tells the BBC.

sentences.text: "I would think, 'I've had awful sleep so I'm going to really struggle today', even if I actually probably had okay sleep.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I was awake the other week for four hours in the night, and my watch was like 'wow, great sleep!' - I literally was awake from 01:00 until 05:00," she says.
