sentences.article_title: Flávio Bolsonaro rides right-wing wave to win first round of Brazil election

sentences.article_title: Flávio Bolsonaro rides right-wing wave to win first round of Brazil election

sentences.article_title: Flávio Bolsonaro rides right-wing wave to win first round of Brazil election

sentences.article_title: Flávio Bolsonaro rides right-wing wave to win first round of Brazil election

sentences.text: Lula faces an extremely difficult task.
sentences.article_title: Flávio Bolsonaro rides right-wing wave to win first round of Brazil election

sentences.article_title: Flávio Bolsonaro rides right-wing wave to win first round of Brazil election

sentences.article_title: Flávio Bolsonaro rides right-wing wave to win first round of Brazil election

sentences.text: The Houthis captured key coastal areas in their recent rapid advance Yemen's civil war has flared up in recent weeks as the Iran-backed Houthi movement, which controls much of the country's north-west, seized large strategically important stretches of the Red Sea coast in a rapid offensive.

sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: Hundreds of people have reportedly been killed on both sides during the Houthis' advance, which came after the collapse of a four-year informal ceasefire.

sentences.text: How escalating Saudi oil crisis could drive up prices everywhere The Houthis are an armed political and religious group from northern Yemen which champions the country's Shia Muslim minority, the Zaidis.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: They declare themselves to be part of the Iranian-led "axis of resistance" against Israel, the US and the wider West - along with armed groups such as Hamas and Lebanon's Hezbollah movement.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: Formally known as the Ansar Allah (Partisans of God), the group emerged in the 1990s and takes its name from the movement's late founder, Hussein al-Houthi.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: His brother, Abdul Malik al-Houthi, has been its de facto leader since 2004.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: In the early 2000s, the Houthis rebelled against Yemen's long-time authoritarian president Ali Abdullah Saleh.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: They wanted greater autonomy for the group's homeland in the north of Yemen.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: The group seized the capital Sanaa after the 2011 Arab Spring, when a popular uprising forced Saleh to hand power to his deputy.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: The Houthis have continued to grow in strength, with troop numbers estimated to have risen to 350,000 last year, and now control between one-quarter and one-third of Yemen's territory, but 70-80% of its population - about 30 million people.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: The group wants an end to a Saudi blockade, control of the whole of Yemen and access to Yemen's oil and gas revenues.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: The Houthis have controlled northern Yemen since 2014 Neighbouring Saudi Arabia feared the Houthis would take over Yemen and make it a satellite of its regional rival, Iran.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: In 2015 Saudi Arabia formed a coalition of Arab countries that intervened on behalf of Yemen's internationally-recognised government.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: But years of air strikes and ground fighting were unable to dislodge the Houthis from most of the territory they seized, and also triggered one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: A temporary ceasefire was brokered in 2022.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: Soon after the start of the Gaza war in October 2023, the Houthis began firing drones and missiles towards Israel and at merchant vessels in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, saying they were acting in support of the Palestinians.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: Western countries deployed warships and the US, UK and Israel carried out air strikes.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: An Israeli strike killed senior Houthi figures including the prime minister of its self-declared government.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: In 2025 the US and the Houthis agreed to stop targeting each other.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: However the Houthis resumed missile attacks on Israel after the US and Israel attacked Iran in February 2026, having paused them after the October 2025 ceasefire in Gaza.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: The informal ceasefire between the Houthis and the Saudis began to unravel in July.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: The Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: They said they were retaliating for what the Houthis say is a years-long Saudi blockade, and for an air strike on Sanaa airport.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: This was followed by a rapid Houthi advance in September that captured as much as 130km (81 miles) of the country's Red Sea coastline as well as the island of Perim.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: The move gave the Houthis significant control of the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait, but they have insisted that they pose no threat to international shipping, except for Saudi-linked vessels.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: The Houthis' actions have caused renewed concern about disruption of world oil supplies.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: Bab al-Mandab has become an increasingly important route for oil exports from Saudi Arabia since shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula, was curtailed due to the US and Israel's war with Iran.

sentences.text: The situation has also been exacerbated by Houthi attacks on Saudi oil installations, as well as an attack on the East-West Pipeline blamed on Iran-backed Iraqi militias, and the escalation threatens to again draw in Western powers.
sentences.article_title: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: A panel of UN experts concluded in 2024 that the Houthis had been transformed into a powerful military organisation due to the transfer of materiel, assistance and training from Iran's Revolutionary Guards, Lebanon's Hezbollah movement and Iraqi specialists.

sentences.text: The volume of oil flowing from the Middle East region has almost returned to pre-war levels, data shows, despite the continued restrictions Iran is placing on vessels attempting to travel through the Strait of Hormuz.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Seven months after the US-Israel war with Iran led to the effective closure of the critical waterway, the maritime intelligence firm Kpler said that in the final week of September, daily oil flow from the Middle East reached 92% of its pre-war baseline.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: About 40% of the total oil exported from the region in September bypassed the strait and exited via overland pipelines to ports on the Red Sea or the Gulf of Oman, up from 17% before the war, according to Kpler.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Oil exports from Iran, on the other hand, have ground to a halt after the reimposition of a US naval blockade in July.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: The US military has been supporting ships as they pass through the Strait of Hormuz since at least mid-June and US Navy data shows the number of vessels assisted by US forces is up by a third in September compared with August.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Martin Kelly, senior intelligence analyst at security firm EOS Risk Group, told BBC Verify that US support is primarily in the form of "air support to ships", including through issuing warnings and intercepting incoming threats from drones, missiles or boats.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: But ships moving through the US-recommended southern route of the strait near the coast of Oman, rather than seeking permission to use Iran's northern route, continue to be targeted.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: September saw the highest number of successful Iranian attacks on commercial shipping since March, according to the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data conflict monitor.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Naveen Das, a senior oil analyst from Kpler, said the oil market "doesn't trust that we're going stay in this status quo" because of the geopolitical risk of further Iranian escalation and the possible impact of the US midterm elections.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Most of the oil passing through the strait now moves via a "shuttle system" of more than 60 large oil tankers moving back and forth, according to Kpler.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: More than 70% of the crude oil which passed through the strait in August was transferred from these "shuttle tankers" onto other vessels in the Gulf of Oman, Kpler said.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: BBC Verify has analysed satellite imagery which appears to show these ship-to-ship transfers, taking place off the coast of the Omani port city, Sohar.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Imagery taken on 24 September shows six pairs of ships docked or paired together near the port, seemingly more protected from Iranian attack.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: But there is "a question over how long these ships can last", said Martin Kelly, particularly as attacks on them continue.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: An average of more than four million barrels of oil per day was transferred from ship to ship in the Gulf of Oman over in the week to 30 September, according to Kpler.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Overall, an average of 12 million barrels of oil per day passed through the strait over this period, compared with a pre-war baseline of 17 million.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Oil exporting countries in the Gulf have also responded to Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz by exporting more crude oil overland via pipelines.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Just under 20% of crude is now leaving the region from ports on the Red Sea at the end of Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline, which is recording exports of more than four million barrels per day, according to Kpler.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Three weeks after an attack on this pipeline blamed on Iran-backed proxies in Iraq, Saudi Arabia is now exporting through the pipeline at "full stretch", according to Kpler.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Almost a quarter of all crude flowing from the region is now being piped past the Strait of Hormuz to terminals along the Gulf of Oman, particularly the city of Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Kpler's data shows.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Naveen Das from Kpler said this increased use of pipelines is likely to become the "new normal" because "it seems very improbable that we live in a world whereby the Gulf countries and Iran go back to being relatively harmonious".
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Oil exports from Iran have fallen almost to zero following the re-imposition of a US blockade in mid-July, down from 1.7 million barrels a day before the war began, Kpler data shows.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: There are 20 empty Iran-flagged tankers currently off the coast of Sri Lanka, unable to return to the Gulf due to the US blockade, according to ship-tracking data and analysis from the US-based advocacy and monitoring organisation United Against Nuclear Iran.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: While crude oil flow from the Middle East has resumed to almost normal levels, exports of liquified natural gas and oil products like jet fuel and have remained well below pre-conflict volumes.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: Fewer than a million barrels of processed oil products passed through the Strait of Hormuz on average in the last week, down from 3.5 million per day before the war began.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons Middle East oil supply is nearly back to pre-Iran war levels

sentences.text: There has been a sharp rise in reports of violence against women and girls in the Gaza Strip, including early and forced marriage, according to a series of recent reports from the UN Population Fund (UNFPA).
sentences.article_title: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds

sentences.text: One report, which analyses data collected by 10 organisations, says , external the protracted crisis in war-torn Gaza has "created conditions in which women and girls face escalating risks of gender-based violence".
sentences.article_title: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds

sentences.text: It also warns that there has been a "severe escalation" in the number of early and forced marriage incidents in the second quarter of this year.
sentences.article_title: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds

sentences.text: Both are considered types of gender-based violence (GBV) by the UN.
sentences.article_title: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds

sentences.text: Another report presenting testimony from 230 women in crowded displacement camps in Gaza City and Khan Younis , external makes for a grim read, describing the violence they have experienced or witnessed.
sentences.article_title: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds

sentences.text: Some readers may find some of the details in this report distressing One displaced woman in a school-turned-shelter in Gaza highlights how rape victims are often married to their rapists to avoid shame and scandal.
sentences.article_title: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds

sentences.text: "When rape cases are discovered in schools, you find weddings and celebrations at the school the next day," she says.
sentences.article_title: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds

sentences.text: Another woman tells how last year, at the time of famine, "a man married off his 14-year-old daughter in exchange for two bags of flour so he and his [other] children could eat".
sentences.article_title: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds

sentences.text: Six women in different displacement camps shared stories of such exchanges - which would have been unthinkable before the conflict between Israel and Hamas began in 2023.
sentences.article_title: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds

sentences.text: Although data collection to establish actual figures remains tricky, in the second quarter of this year, the UNFPA says the number of reported cases of early and forced marriage had increased by 123% on the first quarter.
sentences.article_title: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds

sentences.text: Early or child marriage involved girls aged 12 to 17.
sentences.article_title: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds

sentences.text: "The trends are shocking," says Nestor Owomuhangi, the UNFPA representative to Palestine.
sentences.article_title: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds

sentences.text: He says that the extreme circumstances over the past three years - which have seen tens of thousands of people killed, mass destruction and multiple waves of displacement in Gaza - have broken down social structures, so "everything is eroded... there is no system".

sentences.text: While food markets have reopened, many cannot afford the goods on offer, there is still extreme poverty and hunger with reliance on charitable handouts.

sentences.text: Public services have largely collapsed, and Israeli air strikes have continued despite the ceasefire.

sentences.text: About 1.2 million Palestinians in Gaza are living in tents or makeshift shelters Prior to the war, girls in Gaza outnumbered and outperformed boys at every level of education above primary school.

sentences.text: Now, with prolonged school closures, many children have dropped out of education.
sentences.article_title: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds

sentences.text: For boys there is pressure to find informal work to help support their families, for girls there are heightened issues around safety.

sentences.text: Living among strangers, without privacy, in a socially conservative society, there are complaints of heightened sexual harassment and abuse - many families see marrying their daughters as a way to protect them and preserve modesty.

sentences.text: Democratic control of either chamber would also mean they could use committees to investigate aspects of the Trump presidency.

sentences.text: Corruption allegations, the new White House ballroom and ICE tactics could be subject to scrutiny.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: There is also a debate within the Democratic Party about whether to impeach Trump, which means to bring charges in Congress that will form the basis for a political, not criminal, trial.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: If the Republican Party stays in control of Congress, Trump will be able to keep going with his plans for the remainder of his time in office.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: The president's name is not on the ballot during the midterm elections, though Trump has urged Republicans to pretend that it is by voting for him as an endorsement of his actions so far.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Whichever way the results fall, commentators are likely to use them to make arguments about how voters feel about the direction of the country under Trump's leadership.
